newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament tells Turkey not to gag press.
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament tells Turkey not to gag press.

text.p: The European Parliament said on Thursday it was concerned that the Turkish authorities were trying to muzzle the press, warning this would damage relations between the European Union and Ankara.

"The European Parliament expresses its strong opposition to attempts to restrict freedom of the press in Turkey," the EU's directly elected assembly said in a resolution, which charged that journalists have been imprisoned, abducted and assassinated.
Euro-MPs called on the government in Ankara "to abandon its plans to adopt a new law to restrict freedom of the press, which would damage relations between the EU and Turkey".
The move came only hours after the 15-member bloc's Parliament voted to freeze EU funds worth 53 million Ecus ($66 million) promised to Turkey for 1997 to help set up an EU-Turkey customs union.
Parliament said it was shocked to learn the Turkish police had detained, fined and expelled from Turkey a member of the Danish Parliament, sent there to observe the trial of Kemal Koc.

Koc, a naturalised Dane, was arrested and jailed by Turkish authorities in Ankara on July 9 while attending his brother's funeral and charged with giving economic assistance to the Kurdish Workers' Party (PKK) from Denmark.
The Euro-deputies also condemned Ankara for compiling a black list of "undesirable" EU politicians and urged the EU Council of Ministers to take steps to ensure it was scrapped.
PKK guerrillas have been fighting the Turkish army for independence or autonomy in southeast Turkey since 1984. The fighting has claimed more than 18,500 lives.
Turkey protested to Denmark in March over the holding of a session of the Brussels-based Kurdish parliament in exile in the Danish legislature. ($1=.8015 Ecu)
